punchline: When the world failed to end on schedule, the group that predicted it started phoning newspapers.
thirty_sec: In 1954 Leon Festinger joined a small group sure that a flood would end the world on 21 December. Members had quit jobs and given belongings away. Midnight passed and no saucer came. By morning the leader announced that the group's faith had spared the world, and the group began looking for followers. Festinger called the clash between belief and evidence cognitive dissonance.
